svg.title: Electrically controlled 1×2 optical switch
svg.desc: Editable, annotation-free top-down functional symbol for a Mach–Zehnder optical switch. One centered optical input enters a symmetric splitter and two interferometer arms. A gold electrode and one electrical control terminal represent a voltage-controlled phase shifter in the upper arm; the electrical return is omitted. The arms approach one another in a nominal 50:50 directional output coupler, remaining distinct waveguides, then separate into two optical outputs. A calibrated differential phase selects either output; a pi change exchanges the selected output. The equal-phase splitter and directional coupler require the appropriate static phase bias. Both outputs are drawn identically because no switch state is selected in this symbol. This is a functional schematic, not a fabrication layout: coupling length, gap, bend radii, actuator technology, wavelength band and switching time are unspecified. Reverse-access and radiation modes of the input splitter are omitted. Short external leads, continuous pale gray cladding and blue cores match the component library. There are no fiber outlines, enclosing box, visible labels or background. All artwork is native vector SVG with separate Inkscape layers for cladding, cores and electrical control. Optical port centers: input (16,80), upper output (284,48), lower output (284,112). Electrical terminal center: (126,13).
